How China Is Regulating AI

Tilly Zhang

Gavekal Dragonomics | 13 Nov 2026

China and the US have agreed to have a government dialogue on risks and best practices relating to artificial intelligence models—issues that are on the agenda when the two sides meet at next week’s APEC summit in Shenzhen. But there are big differences in how the two countries approach the regulation of AI, which have become increasingly visible as China has accelerated its rule-setting activity this year.In the US, the AI policy debate is mostly around how to manage the risks of the rapidly advancing capabilities of frontier models, as well as the on-the-ground impact from the construction of data centers and related infrastructure. Neither issue features prominently in Chinese discussions: domestic models are not at the frontier, and infrastructure development is uncontroversial. China’s strategy for AI instead emphasizes the large-scale adoption of models and tools across industries to boost productivity.
